transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Mike Tanaka (CTO - Atlas), Sara Gomez (ML Eng), Dave Lin (Infra), Priya Rao (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Alright hi everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight 30, 40 ish minutes demo and then time for Q&A, my name is Jordan I'm the AE, with me Priya, our SE.
[00:12] Priya: hey hi all, i'll do most of the demo, quick agenda, show API parity mapping, console walkthrough, optimize suggestions for cost/latency, and then discuss private/VPC options.
[00:22] Mike: sounds good, thanks. Our main ask is we need to replace OpenAI and Anthropic calls without changing too much client code, and get similar latency, also concerned about compliance.
[00:34] Priya: totally, thats the common ask, we'll show the mapping table where openai gpt-4o calls map to redwood/gpt4o, anthropic claude-3-ish maps to redwood/claude-compat variants, and together models map to together-compat families. We also cover function-calling differences and streaming.
[00:50] Sara: are the embeddings API compatible? we use text-embedding-3 small from openai heavily for search and rerank.
[00:58] Priya: yes, Redwood exposes embeddings endpoints, we have vector formats compatible out-of-box, but tokenization and embedding dims may differ per model, so parity table notes expected cosine distances and suggested thresholds.
[01:12] Dave: latency profile, we have 99th p95 requirements ~300ms for chat completions, can Redwood hit that?
[01:20] Priya: depends on model and setup; hosted api often hits p95 ~150-400ms for smaller LMs on our optimized runtime, for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated capacity or VPC with reserved GPUs. We also discussed batching and prefix KV cache which reduces cost but can affect tail latency; we can tune autoscaling policies.
[01:40] Mike: ok procurement also wants to know about security, SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO.
[01:46] Jordan: we have SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC in console, audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we offer encrypted at-rest and-in-transit and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private.
[02:05] Priya: quick live demo, i'm going to share my screen, show the API call side-by-side so you can see a drop-in replacement pattern. (screen share noise)
[02:22] [02:22] Priya: ok, here's an example, openai style request with function calling, name: get_invoice, parameters etc — on the right I call Redwood api /v1/chat/completions with model redwood/gpt4o, payload looks very similar, we support function-calling via structured functions array, our SDK has helper wrappers.
[02:45] Sara: any differences in the function-calling payload? like we rely on required fields and the schema enforcement.
[02:50] Priya: almost identical, small differences: our response wraps function call details in 'tool_call' sometimes the field name may be slightly different in older SDKs, but for the current it's parity. There are also edge cases around streaming function-calls where you want partial tool outputs, we stream tokens and then a final tool payload. We'll include a snippet in the parity doc.
[03:10] Dave: what about rate limits, we have spikes from 10k to 50k rps occasionally during batch sends.
[03:17] Jordan: hosted has quota and rate limiting tiers, for that spike we usually recommend Dedicated with autoscaler and burst capacity, or request a custom SLA.
[03:28] Mike: pricing roughness? our finance team will push back if costs jump.
[03:33] Jordan: two levers — model choice (smaller quantized vs full) and batching/cache. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and batching windows that keep cost low while maintaining latency. We'll share sample cost comparisons in the parity sheet.
[03:49] Priya: now console, i open routes page showing per-route token costs and latency heatmap, you can pin rollouts to a canary model variant and automatic fallback to a cheaper model on high load.
[04:02] [04:02] Priya: here's the 'parity mapping' doc link i uploaded (note: will send link in follow up). It lists OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls, parameter mapping, streaming notes, expected output diffs, and recommended prompts adjustments.
[04:20] Sara: about tokenizer diffs, do we need to retune prompts? we saw a slight change in stop-sequence behavior before.
[04:27] Priya: yes sometimes you may need small prompt nudges; the doc flags high-risk prompts. For embeddings we include alignment thresholds and suggested reranking thresholds.
[04:36] Mike: procurement/security question — for on-prem or air-gapped options how much of the control plane stays on-prem?
[04:42] Jordan: for Private we provide customer-managed control plane option; you can run the compute plane in your VPC/on-prem, we still offer an operator package and audit hooks, all keys under your KMS. We'll share architecture docs.
[04:56] Dave: do you support HSM-backed keys?
[04:58] Priya: yes KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated depending on contract. Hosted can do CMEK for enterprise.
[05:06] [05:06] Mike: curious about performance testing — will you run benchmarks for us?
[05:10] Priya: yes we'll run a benchmark using your prompt set if you share it; we'll replicate token lengths and concurrency patterns. We also recommended running a quick pilot on Dedicated for a week.
[05:20] Sara: Are there any known regressions when moving from Anthropic to Redwood? we use Claude for safety/steering.
[05:28] Priya: behavioral differences exist; we have verified 'redwood/claude-compat' for functional parity but safety behaviour can differ, we suggest running evals and Redwood Optimize can highlight quality regressions tied to your prompt set.
[05:42] Jordan: ok quick demo of SDK migration snippet, here's an openai call with openai.ChatCompletion.create, switching is two- three lines using our SDK and endpoint url. Also for streaming we support SSE and websockets similar to what you have now.
[06:05] [06:05] Priya: going through a parity example: OpenAI streaming tokens -> Redwood streaming tokens, notes about partial function-calls, you may need to buffer on client side if you relied on final metadata.
[06:22] Dave: for embeddings, do we support existing ANN index formats? we use Faiss.
[06:26] Priya: yes embeddings are standard float32 vectors, we export in formats compatible with Faiss and other vector stores. We also offer a hosted vector DB add-on but most customers keep Faiss.
[06:38] Mike: timeline — we want to pilot by mid-september, procurement wraps by end of sept.
[06:44] Jordan: that sounds doable, we'll aim to have parity sheet and benchmark results within a week and then schedule pilot kickoff.
[06:52] [06:52] Priya: quick note on quantization — in Dedicated you can run int8 variants, in Redwood Optimize we recommend quantization profile per model based on your prompt length distribution. Helps cut cost 2-3x.
[07:07] Sara: any gotchas with streaming + function calling + embeddings combo? we've seen issues when mixing streaming results and incremental embedding writes.
[07:16] Priya: it's mostly client side orchestration; we recommend that the streaming path emits complete events for functions, and embedding writes triggered on finalization. We'll include code patterns in the parity doc.
[07:28] [07:28] Mike: ok can you send security packet? we'll share with InfoSec.
[07:31] Jordan: yes SOC2, ISO, architecture, KMS docs, and our private deployment guide — will send.
[07:38] Priya: last part, Optimize — console suggestions show batching window, cache TTL, model quantization recommendations, and expected cost delta; you can try simulated workload to see predictions.
[07:50] Dave: curious about autoscaler — does it scale pods or cards? we have GPU card fragmentation concerns.
[07:56] Priya: our autoscaler is GPU-aware and schedules by allocation units, we also support placement policies to avoid fragmentation; for Dedicated we'll work with you on slot sizing.
[08:09] [08:09] Jordan: we're running short on time, let's recap and next steps.
[08:12] Mike: yep go for it.
[08:14] Jordan: recap: 1) Jordan to send parity spreadsheet, demo recording, and security docs by Tue 8/24. 2) Priya to run benchmarks on Atlas staging with your prompts and measure latency/cost by 8/28. 3) Atlas to confirm pilot timeline and provide sample prompts and token metrics by 8/25. 4) schedule pilot kickoff for week of 9/14 if procurement clears.
[08:40] Sara: sounds good thanks for the clear mapping, really helpful.
[08:44] Mike: thanks everyone, excited to see the parity sheet.
[08:47] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email. bye.
